title: Confirm quantity time semantics

Schema/UI impact: keep quantity as descriptive/count metadata and estimated_minutes as total row effort; do not multiply estimated_minutes by quantity in recursive CTEs, daily plan totals, validation, reports, or progress calculations. title: Define production admin access hardening
description: Choose the MVP control for admin surface exposure: IP allowlist, VPN, provider-level access control, or another approved control aligned with SECURITY_RULES.md.
acceptance_criteria: Deployment and routing work has a concrete admin hardening target before production configuration.
notes:
Security recommendation prepared by Subagent 5 on 2026-07-28.

Recommendation:
- Production admin access must have an edge/network-level control in addition to app auth, MFA, server-side role checks, and Supabase RLS. SECURITY_RULES.md says the admin panel must not be publicly exposed without VPN, IP whitelist, or equivalent.
- Preferred production target: route admin functionality under a distinct /admin prefix and protect /admin and any admin-only API/server-action surfaces with Vercel Firewall/WAF custom rules or Vercel Trusted IPs, allowing only approved office/VPN static egress IP/CIDR ranges. Unauthorized traffic should be denied before the Next.js app renders admin UI.
- If the company has no stable office/VPN IP, establish a VPN or access proxy with static egress before production. If no such network control is approved, split admin into a separate admin subdomain/app that can be protected independently.
- Keep app-layer defenses even with edge protection: Supabase Auth aal2 required, server-side admin role checks on every admin route/action, generic errors, no frontend-only protection, RLS least privilege, no service-role key in browser, rate limits and request size limits on auth/admin mutations.

Vercel/Supabase constraints and tradeoffs:
- Vercel Deployment Protection can protect deployments, but current docs indicate Hobby Standard Protection does not protect the production domain; protecting production/all deployments requires Pro/Enterprise features, and Trusted IPs are Enterprise. Password protection is Enterprise or Pro add-on and should not be the sole admin control for a sensitive production admin panel.
- Vercel WAF custom rules are available on all plans and can act on request path and client/IP-related parameters, with deny/challenge/rate-limit style actions. This is the best low-cost candidate if it can express the required path + allowlisted IP condition for /admin in the selected plan.
- Vercel Trusted IPs are the cleanest provider-level IP allowlist for production, but Enterprise-only according to current docs.
- Supabase RLS protects data even if app routes are reached, but RLS is not a substitute for the SECURITY_RULES.md requirement that the admin panel surface itself not be publicly exposed.

MVP posture:
- During local/dev/preview: admin app must still require Supabase login, admin role, and aal2 MFA. Preview deployments should use Vercel Authentication / Deployment Protection where available.
- Before production: do not launch admin routes publicly until one approved edge/network hardening approach is configured and verified.

Production posture options for human selection:
1. Recommended: stable company VPN or office static IP + Vercel WAF custom rule denying /admin and admin API paths unless source IP/CIDR is allowlisted. Lowest practical cost if WAF condition coverage is sufficient.
2. Stronger/provider-native: Vercel Enterprise Trusted IPs for production deployments, preferably with VPN static egress. Cleanest Vercel-native match to SECURITY_RULES.md, but likely paid/Enterprise.
3. Identity-provider access layer: Vercel All Deployments / Vercel Authentication / SAML SSO if the app can be restricted to authorized Vercel/team/IdP users. This may be unsuitable for employee app access and may require Pro/Enterprise/add-ons.
4. Separate admin surface: deploy admin on a separate subdomain/app behind an approved access proxy/VPN, while employee app remains normally reachable after app auth. Higher architecture complexity, clearer isolation.

Rejected as sole controls:
- Hiding admin links in the UI.
- Next.js middleware or server-side auth alone without edge/network hardening.
- Password protection alone for production admin access.
- Supabase RLS alone as a substitute for admin route exposure hardening.

Human decision request:
- Choose one production control before closing this issue: A) stable VPN/static IP plus Vercel WAF rule, B) Vercel Enterprise Trusted IPs, C) Vercel Pro/Enterprise Deployment Protection/SSO model, or D) separate admin subdomain/app behind an approved access proxy.
- Confirm whether nobleclean has a stable office IP or can provide a VPN/static egress IP.
- Confirm whether the project may use paid Vercel features if required. Current PRD says zero ongoing cost, which conflicts with some strongest Vercel-native production protection options.

Implementation acceptance target after human choice:
- Admin routes and admin API/action endpoints have a documented, tested edge/network block before app auth.
- Authenticated admin access still requires aal2 MFA and server/database authorization.
- Verification includes browser checks for allowed and denied access paths and review of Vercel Firewall/Deployment Protection settings.

Sources consulted:
- _handoff/NobleClean-Ops_PRD.md, _handoff/SECURITY_RULES.md, _handoff/PROJECT_STRATEGY.md, _handoff/AI_ENVIRONMENT.md, _handoff/PROGRESS.md, AGENTS.md.

- Vercel Trusted IPs: https://vercel.com/docs/deployment-protection/methods-to-protect-deployments/trusted-ips
- Vercel WAF/Firewall: https://vercel.com/docs/vercel-firewall and https://vercel.com/docs/vercel-firewall/vercel-waf/custom-rules
- Vercel WAF rule reference: https://vercel.com/docs/vercel-firewall/vercel-waf/rule-configuration
- Vercel two-factor enforcement: https://vercel.com/docs/two-factor-enforcement
- Supabase MFA and RLS docs: https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/auth-mfa and https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security
close_reason: Resolved production admin access hardening target: protect /admin and future admin-only API paths with Vercel WAF VPN/static-egress IP allowlisting, or approved equivalent; documented in AUTH_SECURITY_CONTROLS, LAUNCH_CHECKLIST, PROJECT_STRATEGY, and PROGRESS.

title: Define MFA rollout policy
description: Decide whether MFA is mandatory for both admin and employees at MVP launch, or admin-only first with a documented employee rollout path.
acceptance_criteria: Auth implementation has a clear MFA requirement before login and account-management work begins.
notes:
Security recommendation prepared by Subagent 5 on 2026-07-28.

Recommendation:
- MVP policy should require MFA for both admin and employees before access to operational data. Admin-only MFA is rejected because SECURITY_RULES.md explicitly requires MFA/2FA for users and admins, and this is an internal app where employee accounts can still expose client assignments, schedules, section/item data, completion history, and uploaded reference images.
- Use Supabase Auth MFA with authenticator-app TOTP as the MVP factor. TOTP is free on Supabase projects and avoids SMS cost, phone-number collection, SIM-swap risk, and extra GDPR data.
- Login flow: after email/password sign-in, check Supabase authenticator assurance level. If current session is aal1 and the user has no verified factor, force enrollment before entering the app. If next level can become aal2, redirect to MFA challenge. Only aal2 sessions may enter admin or employee app areas.
- Database enforcement: add restrictive RLS policies requiring (select auth.jwt()->>'aal') = 'aal2' for app tables that expose operational data. This should be defense in depth in addition to server-side route/action checks. Do not rely on frontend redirects only.
- Admin posture: admin must have MFA before any admin CRUD/reporting access. Admin factor unenrollment must require aal2 and should not be self-service if it would leave the account without a verified factor.
- Employee posture: employees must enroll MFA during first login before seeing client data. Provide a short German/English enrollment flow and a manager-assisted recovery process for lost devices.

Risk tradeoffs:
- Mandatory employee MFA adds onboarding friction and recovery support, but it prevents account takeover from weak/reused passwords and aligns with SECURITY_RULES.md.
- TOTP is less convenient than SMS for some staff, but it is more private, cheaper, and safer than phone-based OTP.
- RLS aal2 checks may temporarily block users with stale JWTs after factor changes; implementation should refresh the session and route users to a challenge/enrollment screen rather than showing a raw 403.

MVP posture:
- TOTP MFA mandatory for all active users: admin and employee.
- No optional employee rollout phase.
- No public self-registration. Accounts are created/invited by admin only.
- Generic auth errors, login rate limiting, secure cookies, and server/database authorization remain mandatory under separate implementation issues.

Production posture:
- Keep MFA mandatory for all app users.
- Require Vercel team 2FA for deploy/admin platform access.
- Require Supabase organization MFA if the selected Supabase plan supports it; at minimum all Supabase project owners/admins must enable MFA.
- Document recovery/runbook before launch: identity verification by company owner/manager, factor reset by trusted admin only, and security event logging for reset/unlock events.

Human approval needed:
- No product decision remains on whether MFA is required; SECURITY_RULES.md decides this as mandatory for all users.
- Human approval is still needed before production for the operational recovery process and employee onboarding communication, but this should not block auth implementation.

Sources consulted:
- _handoff/NobleClean-Ops_PRD.md, _handoff/SECURITY_RULES.md, _handoff/PROJECT_STRATEGY.md, _handoff/AI_ENVIRONMENT.md, _handoff/PROGRESS.md, AGENTS.md.
- Supabase MFA docs: https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/auth-mfa and https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/auth-mfa/totp
- Supabase RLS docs including MFA aal claim example: https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security
- Supabase org MFA enforcement: https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/mfa/org-mfa-enforcement
- Vercel team 2FA enforcement: https://vercel.com/docs/two-factor-enforcement
close_reason: Decision resolved by SECURITY_RULES.md and Supabase MFA/RLS capability: MFA mandatory for admin and employees at MVP using TOTP, with aal2 enforced in app/server/RLS.

title: Review free-tier backup and storage limits
description: Review Supabase and Vercel free-tier backup, storage, connection, and retention limits against expected NobleClean-Ops usage and GDPR expectations.
acceptance_criteria: Production launch checklist includes any required paid-tier upgrade triggers or risk acceptance.
notes:
Research date: 2026-07-28. Scope: official Supabase and Vercel sources only. No secrets read, no Supabase/Vercel MCP connected.

Decision summary for NobleClean-Ops:
- Supabase Free may be acceptable only for a very small pre-launch/MVP pilot if management accepts manual off-site backup responsibility, limited log/audit retention, 500 MB DB cap, 1 GB storage cap, and no automatic backups/PITR.
- Vercel Hobby should not be used for NobleClean-Ops production because Vercel Terms restrict Hobby to personal/non-commercial use and allow Hobby projects/deployments to be disabled/removed at Vercel's discretion. NobleClean-Ops is a business/internal company operations tool, so production should use at least Vercel Pro or another paid business-appropriate hosting plan.
- Before public/production launch with employee/client operational data, legal/privacy owner must sign/obtain applicable DPAs and confirm international transfer posture. This is technical planning, not legal approval.

Supabase Free limits found:
- Pricing/free included usage: 50,000 MAU, 500 MB database, shared CPU/500 MB RAM, 5 GB uncached egress + 5 GB cached egress, 1 GB file storage, 2 active free projects, free projects paused after 1 week inactivity. Source: https://supabase.com/pricing
- Billing docs list Free usage items: 5 GB egress, 500 MB DB, 50,000 MAU, 1 GB storage, 500,000 Edge Function invocations, 2M Realtime messages, 200 Realtime peak connections. Source: https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/billing-on-supabase
- Storage upload max file size on Free: 50 MB global file size cap; bucket-specific caps can be lower. Source: https://supabase.com/docs/guides/storage/uploads/file-limits
- Bandwidth/egress: Free organizations have 10 GB total bandwidth split as 5 GB cached + 5 GB uncached; includes transfer from database, storage, and functions. Source: https://supabase.com/docs/guides/storage/serving/bandwidth
- Compute/DB performance: Nano/free compute is shared CPU, up to 0.5 GB memory, recommended max DB size 500 MB; baseline disk throughput 5 MB/s and 250 baseline IOPS; max direct DB connections 60 and pooler clients 200. Source: https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/compute-and-disk
- Connection guidance: serverless/temporary clients should use pooler transaction mode; direct connection is mainly for migrations, pg_dump, long-lived backend. Source: https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/connecting-to-postgres
- Backups: Supabase automatic daily backups are for Pro/Team/Enterprise. Free-tier projects should regularly export with Supabase CLI `db dump` and maintain off-site backups. Storage API objects are not included in database backups. PITR is paid and requires at least Pro plus Small compute add-on. Source: https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/backups
- Security/compliance: Supabase states SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, encryption at rest/in transit, and paid-database backups; DPA must be requested/signed through Supabase dashboard to be legally binding. Sources: https://supabase.com/security and https://supabase.com/legal/dpa

Vercel Hobby/Free limits and constraints found:
- Hobby is free but intended for personal projects/small-scale apps. Included usage includes 100 GB Fast Data Transfer, 10 GB Fast Origin Transfer, 1M function invocations, 1M Edge Requests, 6,000 build minutes, 100 deployments/day, 1 concurrent build, 45 min max build time/deployment, 10s default function duration configurable up to 60s, 1 hour runtime logs up to 4,000 rows. Sources: https://vercel.com/docs/plans/hobby and https://vercel.com/docs/limits
- Account plans docs: Hobby deployments may be paused after hitting included usage; Pro/Enterprise continue with on-demand usage instead. Source: https://vercel.com/docs/plans
- Pricing FAQ: Hobby is personal/non-commercial; free Hobby accounts cannot purchase additional usage. Source: https://vercel.com/pricing
- Terms: Hobby plan is for personal/non-commercial use; Vercel may change/discontinue Hobby terms and may disable/remove Hobby projects/deployments with or without notice. Source: https://vercel.com/legal/terms
- Deployment protection: Vercel Authentication is available on all plans; Password Protection requires Enterprise or Pro + Advanced Deployment Protection add-on; Trusted IPs are Enterprise only. Source: https://vercel.com/docs/deployment-protection/methods-to-protect-deployments
- Deployment protection bypass: Shareable Links and automation bypass are available on all plans; Deployment Protection Exceptions require Enterprise or Pro + Advanced Deployment Protection add-on. Source: https://vercel.com/docs/deployment-protection/methods-to-bypass-deployment-protection
- Vercel security/DPA: Vercel states encryption at rest/in transit and DDoS mitigation; Vercel DPA applies to Enterprise and Pro customers, not Hobby. Sources: https://vercel.com/security and https://vercel.com/legal/dpa

Launch risks for NobleClean-Ops:
1. Vercel Hobby is not suitable for production business use because of non-commercial terms and discretionary suspension/removal risk.
2. Supabase Free has no automatic backups; manual DB dumps are not enough for a GDPR-sensitive operational production system unless there is a documented backup schedule, restore test, storage-object backup/export plan, and management risk acceptance.
3. Supabase DB backups do not include Storage objects, so reference images need a separate backup/export procedure even on paid plans.
4. Supabase Free log retention and lack of platform audit logs are weak for incident investigation, access review, and GDPR accountability.
5. Supabase Free 1 GB storage can be exhausted quickly if admins upload original camera photos; app must compress/resize/reference-image uploads and enforce strict per-file caps.
6. Supabase Free 500 MB DB cap is probably OK for initial internal use, but completion history grows indefinitely; retention/anonymization policy is needed before launch.
7. Supabase Nano connection limits are fine for low traffic if using Supabase client/Data API/pooler correctly; avoid direct DB connections from serverless runtime except migrations/backups.
8. Deployment protection on Vercel Hobby/standard controls does not replace application auth/RLS. Production admin route hardening still needs app-level auth, server-side authorization, MFA policy, CSP/security headers, and ideally business-plan controls.

Upgrade / mitigation triggers:
- Upgrade Vercel to Pro before any production use by nobleclean or employees because the app is commercial/business internal software.
- Upgrade Supabase to Pro before production if management requires provider-managed automatic backups, 7-day backup retention, email support, non-pausing project behavior, larger DB/storage/egress headroom, or a signed DPA-backed launch posture.
- Add Supabase PITR only when recovery point objective must be better than daily/manual backups, or after real operational data becomes business-critical enough that losing same-day changes is unacceptable.
- Move beyond Supabase Free immediately if DB size exceeds 350 MB sustained or is projected to exceed 500 MB within 30 days; if storage exceeds 700 MB sustained or image growth projects to exceed 1 GB within 30 days; if egress reaches 70% of cached/uncached quota; if realtime peak connections approach 150; if DB connection usage approaches 45 direct or 150 pooler clients; or if any free-tier restriction causes service degradation.
- Require image upload limits before launch: allowlisted image types, magic-byte validation, random object names, compression/resizing target well below 50 MB, storage bucket policies/RLS, and separate storage backup/export procedure.
- Require monthly restore drills while on Free/manual backups; move to paid managed backups if restore testing is not operationally owned.

Recommendation for launch checklist nobleclean-kja.2:
- Mark Vercel Pro as required for production launch.
- Treat Supabase Free only as pilot/staging unless owner signs explicit risk acceptance covering manual backups, no automatic backups/PITR, limited logs/audit, and storage-object backup responsibility.
- Before launch: choose EU Supabase region where appropriate, execute Supabase and Vercel DPAs if using paid plans, document subprocessors in nobleclean privacy materials, define data retention/erasure/anonymization rules, and confirm GDPR legal review.
close_reason: Official Supabase/Vercel free-tier research recorded in issue notes with launch risks and upgrade triggers.

title: Confirm status token semantics
description: Confirm that status-success is reserved for completion/system success and status-recent is used for recently cleaned advisory state.
acceptance_criteria: Decision is recorded before badge component and status indicator logic are implemented.
notes: Subagent 4 recommendation (2026-07-28): Keep status-success reserved for system/completion confirmations and status-recent reserved for the recently cleaned advisory state. Rationale: PRD Section 6.1 explicitly separates item advisory states from system success states; this prevents employees/admins from confusing 'completed/submitted successfully' with 'normal item is not urgent because it was cleaned within recurrence window'. Schema/UI impact: Priority/Status Badge should support high_priority/status-critical, complaint/status-warning, recent/status-recent, and separate system success/status-success variants. Leaf-item urgency logic must never emit status-success; system workflows such as submitted, fully completed, saved, or dashboard success may use status-success. Normal items outside recurrence should show no badge. Exact human decision needed: approve the split 'status-success = system completion only; status-recent = recently cleaned advisory only' before badge/theme tokens and status indicator logic are implemented.
close_reason: Decision recorded: status-success is reserved for system/completion success states only. status-recent is the recently-cleaned advisory token. Leaf-item urgency/status logic must never emit status-success; normal items outside recurrence show no badge.
